items.title: Harvest from six registries
items.text: Bioregistry, OBO Foundry, OLS, TIB, LOV and NeuroSchema, merged into one record per resource, with every field traced to its source.

items.title: Discovery beyond registries
items.text: prefix.cc, w3id.org, Zenodo, GitHub and suggested URLs are probed by content negotiation, and only real ontologies, vocabularies and schemas are accepted.

items.title: Reproducible downloads
items.text: Each registry download is archived with its checksum, so the catalog can be rebuilt offline, and a single registry can be refreshed on its own.

items.title: Submissions through GitHub
items.text: The submission form opens an issue that a bot turns into a pull request, with link, DOI and registry checks on every change.

items.title: Rubric v4: source-neutral scoring
items.text: A check whose only evidence source doesn't cover a resource is "not assessed" instead of failed, and no problem is penalised twice.

items.title: Our own quality checks
items.text: ROBOT (report, ELK reasoner, OWL 2 DL profile) and OOPS! pitfall scans run on every ontology, with the OBO Dashboard shown side by side for comparison.

items.title: DOI verification across services
items.text: Reference DOIs are checked against Crossref, DataCite, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and doi.org.

items.title: Quality checks for every ontology
items.text: ROBOT (report, ELK reasoner, OWL 2 DL profile), pitfall scans and import reading run on every ontology with a download, several at a time. A full pass resumes where it stopped, and each run reports how many ontologies have been checked.

items.title: Read imports from the artefact
items.text: owl:imports and the terms an ontology uses are read from the file itself, so upper-ontology alignment (BFO, COB, DOLCE, GFO, gUFO), RO use and vocabulary reuse are measured for every checked ontology, not only those listed in OLS or Bioregistry (rubric v4.1).

items.title: Rubric validation
items.text: A published report of how sensitive grades are to the weights (random and one-at-a-time changes), how well our quality checks agree with the OBO Dashboard, and how scores compare with expert ratings.

items.title: Metrics across runs
items.text: Each resource's page shows how its score, every criterion and the quality metrics changed from one evaluation run to the next.

items.title: Expert ratings
items.text: Collecting ratings from domain experts to compare with our scores. Get in touch if you'd like to rate resources in your field.

items.title: Adoption evidence beyond OBO
items.text: Count adopting projects from papers, software dependencies and data repositories, not only curated entries and OBO Foundry usages.

items.title: Community standards per domain
items.text: Score R1.3 against each field's own standards bodies and principles, not only the OBO Foundry's.

items.title: Flag disagreements between portals
items.text: Our checks are already shown next to the OBO Dashboard's on each page. Next: highlight where OLS, TIB and BioPortal report different versions or class counts.

items.title: Papers that cite each resource
items.text: Collect citing papers from OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and Crossref, with citation counts over time on each resource's page.

items.title: Papers that use a resource
items.text: Find papers that use a resource in their methods or data, not just cite it, to give adoption evidence across fields.

items.title: New publications
items.text: Detect new reference papers and versions of a resource and suggest them as catalog updates.

items.title: Similar resources
items.text: Suggest related resources on each page, based on domain, shared imports and overlapping terms.

items.title: Which ontology should I use?
items.text: A guided finder that recommends well-maintained, well-scored resources for a domain, data type or task.

items.title: Alternatives to inactive resources
items.text: Point to active replacements when a resource is archived, deprecated or no longer maintained.

items.title: MCP server
items.text: AI assistants can search the catalog, read a resource's score with the evidence behind each point, follow its history across runs, and get the scoring rubric, through a Model Context Protocol server authenticated with a personal access token. Setup on the API & MCP page.

items.title: Machine-readable catalog and API
items.text: A documented JSON API (OpenAPI) for search with facets, entries, history, runs and statistics, plus JSON and JSON-LD (DCAT, schema.org) downloads. The site itself is built from the same API.

items.title: llms.txt and AI-friendly pages
items.text: An llms.txt index and plain-text summaries of each resource and the rubric, so language models read the catalog accurately and cite it.

items.title: AI-readiness checks
items.text: Measure how ready each resource is for use in AI pipelines: definitions and labels on its terms, synonyms, machine-readable downloads, stable IRIs and a license that allows reuse.

items.title: Semantic search
items.text: Search by meaning across resource descriptions and term definitions, not only keywords, to find the right ontology for a concept.

items.title: Sign in with GitHub
items.text: Sign in with your GitHub account. Submissions and corrections are credited to you on the GitHub issue, and you can follow them on your account page.

items.title: Personal access tokens and rate limits
items.text: Create scoped, expiring, revocable tokens for the API and for MCP clients. Anonymous use is limited per IP; signed-in users and tokens get a much higher limit.

items.title: Activity and audit log
items.text: Every sign-in, sign-out, token change, submission and data load is recorded with who, what and when. You can see your own activity; administrators see everything and can adjust rate limits.

items.title: Easier submissions
items.text: Projects that use a resource are entered one per row instead of a formatted text box, and the form checks each one before you submit.

items.title: Score badges
items.text: An embeddable badge with the current grade for READMEs and websites.

items.title: Improvement reports
items.text: A per-resource checklist of the changes that would raise its score the most, such as a PURL, a license or a version IRI.

items.title: Change alerts
items.text: Opt-in notices when a resource's links break or its score drops.
